title: Minimum Number of Operations to Make All Array Elements Equal to 1
summary: Given a 0-indexed array of positive integers, you can perform operations where you select an index i (0 <= i < n-1) and replace either nums[i] or nums[i+1] with their gcd.
statement: Given a 0-indexed array of positive integers, you can perform operations where you select an index i (0 <= i < n-1) and replace either nums[i] or nums[i+1] with their gcd. Determine the minimum number of operations needed to make all array elements equal to 1, or return -1 if impossible. The gcd of two integers is the largest integer that divides both without a remainder.
constraints: In one operation, choose adjacent values and replace either one with their greatest common divisor.
Return the minimum operations needed to make every value one.
Return -1 when no sequence can create a one.
reference_solution:
def minimum_operations_to_all_ones(nums):
    import math
    ones=nums.count(1);n=len(nums)
    if ones:return n-ones
    shortest=n+1
    for left in range(n):
        common=0
        for right in range(left,n):
            common=math.gcd(common,nums[right])
            if common==1:shortest=min(shortest,right-left+1);break
    return -1 if shortest>n else n+shortest-2

hints: Existing ones convert each non-one neighbor in one operation, so handle that case directly.
Otherwise find the shortest contiguous subarray whose gcd is one.
It takes length-1 operations to create one there, then n-1 operations to spread it through the array.
Any first one must arise from a contiguous chain of gcd operations, so the shortest gcd-one subarray is necessary and sufficient.
